what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains two medicines working together: valsartan, which relaxes your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, and hydrochlorothiazide, a water pill (diuretic) that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body. Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food, once a day. Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. If you need to split the tablet, ask your pharmacist if your tablet can be cut, as not all strengths are scored.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you based on your blood pressure and other health conditions. Common starting doses include valsartan 80 mg or 160 mg combined with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, taken once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, contact your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it in the original container, away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium, or other potassium-containing products without asking your doctor, as valsartan can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and cause dizziness or fainting. Be careful when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position, especially when you first start this medicine, as it may cause dizziness. Avoid excessive sun exposure and tanning beds, as hydrochlorothiazide can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid anti-inflammatory pain relievers (such as ibuprofen or naproxen) unless your doctor approves, as they can reduce the effectiveness of this medicine and affect your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; signs of low sodium such as headache, confusion, weakness, or seizures; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, or decreased urination; or if your blood pressure remains high despite taking this medicine as directed.
when_it_works: You may start to see some blood pressure lowering within the first week of treatment. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Even if you feel well, keep taking it every day as prescribed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so it is important not to stop the medicine just because you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as both ingredients may pass into breast milk and could harm your baby. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering and diuretic effects of this medicine, which may increase the risk of dizziness and falls. Use caution when changing positions and report any dizziness to your doctor. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children. Diabetic patients: Hydrochlorothiazide may affect blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar closely and report any changes to your doctor.
